headings: Statistical Disclosure by Bank Holding Companies
paragraphs: Cass Information Systems, Inc. ("Cass" or the "Company") provides payment and information processing services to large manufacturing, distribution and retail enterprises across the United States. The Company's services include freight invoice rating, payment processing, auditing, and the generation of accounting and transportation information. Cass also processes and pays facility-related invoices, which include electricity and gas as well as waste and telecommunications expenses. Cass solutions include integrated payments, a B2B payment platform for clients that require an agile fintech partner. Additionally, the Company offers a church management software solution and an on-line platform to provide generosity services for faith-based and non-profit organizations. The Company's bank subsidiary, Cass Commercial Bank (the "Bank"), supports the Company's payment operations. The Bank also provides banking services to its target markets, which include privately held businesses in the St. Louis metropolitan area and restaurant franchises and faith-based ministries within the United States.

On April 7, 2025, the Company signed an Asset Purchase Agreement providing for the sale of its telecom expense management and managed mobility solutions business unit ("TEM Business Unit") to Asignet USA Inc ("Asignet") for a purchase price of $18.0 million. The sale closed on June 30, 2025. The Company also signed a Transition Services Agreement with Asignet to provide certain information technology, data ingestion, and payment processing services for a period of time not to exceed 18 months after closing.

Cass is an information services company with a primary focus on processing payables and payables-related transactions for large corporations located in the United States. Cass possesses four core competencies that encompass most of its processing services.

Data acquisition – This refers to the gathering of data elements from diverse, heterogeneous sources and the building of complete databases for our customers. Data is the raw material of the information economy. Cass gathers vital data from complex and diverse input documents, electronic media, proprietary databases and data feeds, including data acquired from vendor invoices as well as customer procurement and sales systems. Through its numerous methods of obtaining streams and pieces of raw data, including those supported by artificial intelligence ("AI"), Cass is able to assemble vital data into centralized data management systems and warehouses, thus producing an engine to create the power of information for managing critical corporate functions and processing systems.

Data management – Once data is assembled, Cass is able to utilize the power from derived information to produce significant savings and benefits for its clients. This information is integrated into customers' unique financial and accounting systems, eliminating the need for internal accounting processing and providing internal and external support for these critical systems. Information is also used to produce management and exception reporting for operational control, feedback, planning assistance and performance measurement.

Business Intelligence – Receiving information in the right place at the right time and in the required format is paramount for business survival. Cass' information delivery solutions provide reports, digital images, data files and retrieval capabilities through the internet or directly into customer internal systems. Cass' proprietary internet management delivery system is the foundation for driving these critical functions. Transaction, operational, control, status and processing exception information are all delivered through this system creating an efficient, accessible and highly reliable asset for Cass customers.

Financial exchange – Since Cass is unique among its competition in that it owns a commercial bank, it is also able to manage the movement of funds from its customers to their suppliers. This is a distinguishing factor, which clearly requires the processing capability, operating systems and financial integrity of a banking organization. Cass provides immediate, accurate, controlled and protected funds management and transfer system capabilities for all of its customers. Old and costly check processing and delivery mechanisms are replaced with more efficient electronic cash management and funds transfer systems.

Cass' core competencies allow it to perform the highest volumes of transaction processing in an integrated, efficient and systematic approach. Not only is Cass able to process the transaction, it is also able to collect the data defining the transaction and effect the financial payment governing its terms.

These core competencies, enhanced through shared business processes, drive Cass' strategic business units. Building upon these foundations, Cass continues to explore new business opportunities that leverage these competencies and processes.

The Company, through its Transportation Information Services business unit, is one of the largest firms in the transportation bill processing and payment industry in the United States based on the total dollars of transportation bills paid and items processed. Competition consists of a few primary competitors and numerous small transportation bill audit firms located throughout the United States. While offering transportation payment services, few of these audit firms compete on a national basis. These competitors compete mainly on price, functionality and service levels. The Company, through its Facilities Expense Management business unit, also competes with other companies located throughout the United States that pay utility bills and provide management reporting. Available data indicates that the Company is one of the largest providers of utility information processing and payment services. Cass is unique among these competitors in that it is not exclusively affiliated with any one energy service provider ("ESP"). Various ESPs market the Company's services, adding value with their unique auditing, consulting and technological capabilities. Many of Cass' services are customized for the ESPs, providing a full-featured solution without any development costs to the ESP. The Company's TouchPoint division offers a church management software solution and an on-line platform to provide generosity services for faith-based and non-profit organizations, which is a complementary service offering to the Bank's faith-based customers. Also, the Company, through its CassPay operation, competes with providers of corporate payment solutions.

The Bank is organized as a Missouri trust company with banking powers and was founded in 1906. The Company was originally classified as a bank holding corporation due to its ownership of a federally-insured commercial bank and was originally organized in 1982 as Cass Commercial Corporation under the laws of Missouri. Approval by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System was received in February 1983. The Company changed its name to Cass Information Systems, Inc. in January 2001. In December 2011, the Federal Reserve Bank ("FRB") of St. Louis approved the election of Cass Information Systems, Inc. to become a financial holding company. As a financial holding company, Cass may engage in activities that are financial in nature or incidental to a financial activity. The Bank encounters competition from numerous banks and financial institutions located throughout the St. Louis, Missouri metropolitan area and other areas in which the Bank competes. The Bank's principal competitors, however, are large bank holding companies that are able to offer a wide range of banking and related services through extensive branch networks. The Bank targets its services to privately held businesses, restaurant franchises, and faith-based ministries located in St. Louis, Missouri and other selected cities located throughout the United States.

The Company holds several trademarks for the payment and rating services it provides. These include: FreightPay®, Transdata®, Ratemaker®, Best Rate®, Rate Exchange®, CassPort®, Cass Freight Index®, Cass Truckload Linehaul Index®, Cass Intermodal Price Index® Expense$mart®, ExpenseSmart®, TouchPoint®, Gyve®, Generosity Made Simple®, WasteVision™, AcuAudit™ and Direct2Carrier Payments™. The Company holds patents for methods and systems of the following: managing employee-liable expenses, communicating expense management information, electronic auditing, and electronically generating and analyzing shipping parameters. The Company also holds patents for computer readable media for electronic auditing.
The Company and its subsidiaries have a varied client base and are not dependent on any one customer or group of customers for a significant portion of its business.

The Company and its subsidiaries had 860 full-time and 156 part-time employees as of February 27, 2026, exclusive of discontinued operations. Of these employees, the Bank had 68 full-time and no part-time employees.

headings: Risks from fluctuating conditions in the financial markets and economic and political conditions generally affect the Company
Unfavorable developments concerning customer credit quality could affect Cass' financial results.
The Company's allowance for credit losses ("ACL") is subject to continuing evaluation and may be insufficient.
Fluctuations in interest rates could affect Cass' net interest income and balance sheet.

In certain circumstances, Cass remits payment of invoices prior to receiving funds from its customers. As such, Cass could experience losses if such funds are not received from customers after payment is remitted.
Cass uses AI in connection with its business and operations, which exposes the Company to inherent risks that may expose it to material harm.
The Company is exposed to risks associated with the handling of customer funds.
The Company may be adversely impacted by changing oil and overall energy prices.
The Company may be adversely impacted by changing freight rates.
Interruptions or performance problems associated with the Company's network technology and infrastructure may adversely affect its business and operating results.
Operational difficulties or cybersecurity problems could damage Cass' reputation and business.
Cass must respond to rapid technological changes and these changes may be more difficult or expensive than anticipated.
Methods of reducing risk exposures might not be effective.
Customer borrowing, repayment, investment, deposit, and payable processing practices may be different than anticipated.
Competitive product and pricing pressure within Cass' markets may change.
Management's ability to maintain and expand customer relationships may differ from expectations.
The Company is subject to liquidity risk.
Management's ability to retain key officers and employees may change.
Cass' stock price can become volatile and fluctuate widely in response to a variety of factors.
The Company is subject to extensive government regulation and supervision and possible enforcement or other legal actions that could detrimentally affect Cass' business.
Cass is subject to examinations and challenges by tax authorities, which, if not resolved in the Company's favor, could adversely affect the Company's financial condition and results of operations.
The value of the Company's goodwill and other intangible assets may decline in the future.
Climate change could have a material negative impact on the Company and its clients.
paragraphs: This section highlights specific risks that could affect the Company's business. Although this section attempts to highlight key factors, please be aware that other risks may prove to be important in the future. New risks may emerge at any time, and Cass cannot predict such risks or estimate the extent to which they may affect the Company's financial performance. This section describes the Company's beliefs regarding the factors that could materially and adversely affect the Company and its business, financial condition and results of operations in the future. All references to past events are intended to be examples only rather than a complete listing or a representation regarding whether such events have occurred in the past or whether they are likely to occur in the future.
In addition to the factors discussed elsewhere or incorporated by reference in this report, the identified risks that could cause actual results to differ materially include the following:

The Company's success depends, to a certain extent, upon local, national and global economic and political conditions, as well as governmental monetary policies. A favorable business environment is generally characterized by, among other factors, economic growth, efficient capital markets, low inflation, low unemployment, high business and investor confidence, and strong business earnings. Unfavorable or uncertain economic and market conditions can be caused by a decline in economic growth both in the U.S. and internationally; declines in business activity or investor or business confidence; limitations on the availability of or increases in the cost of credit and capital; increases in inflation or interest rates; high unemployment; oil price volatility; natural disasters; trade policies and tariffs; or a combination of these or other factors. In addition, financial markets and global supply chains may be adversely affected by the current or anticipated impact of global wars/military conflicts, terrorism or other geopolitical events. Current economic conditions are being heavily impacted by recent inflationary conditions and higher interest rates, the effects of which may impact the Company's profitability by negatively impacting its fixed costs and expenses. Economic and inflationary pressure on consumers and uncertainty regarding economic improvement could result in changes in consumer and business spending, borrowing and savings habits. Such conditions could have a material adverse effect on the credit quality of the Company's loans and its business, financial condition and results of operations.

Federal budget deficit concerns and the potential for political conflict over legislation to fund U.S. government operations and raise the U.S. government's debt limit may increase the possibility of a default by the U.S. government on its debt obligations, related credit-rating downgrades, or an economic recession in the United States. Many of the Company's investment securities are issued by the U.S. government and government agencies and sponsored entities. As a result of uncertain domestic political conditions, including potential future federal government shutdowns, the possibility of the federal government defaulting on its obligations for a period of time due to debt ceiling limitations or other unresolved political issues, investments in financial instruments issued or guaranteed by the federal government pose liquidity risks. Most recently, in connection with successive failures by the U.S. government to reverse the trend of large annual fiscal deficits and growing interest costs, Moody's lowered its long-term issuer credit rating on the U.S. from Aaa to Aa1. A further downgrade, or downgrades by other rating agencies, as well as sovereign debt issues facing the governments of
other countries, could have a material adverse impact on financial markets and economic conditions in the U.S. and worldwide.

Certain events beyond the Company's control, such as severe weather, natural disasters, terrorist activities or other hostilities, may adversely affect the general economy, financial and capital markets, specific industries, and the Company.

paragraphs: The specific payment and information processing services provided to each customer are developed individually to meet each customer's requirements, which can vary greatly. In addition, the degree of automation such as electronic data interchange, imaging, work flow, and web-based solutions varies greatly among customers and industries. These factors combine so that pricing varies greatly among the customer base. In general, however, Cass is compensated for its processing services through service fees, transactional level payment services, and investment of account balances generated during the payment process. The amount, type, and calculation of service fees vary greatly by service offering, but generally follow the volume of transactions processed. Transactional level payment services and interest income from the balances generated during the payment processing cycle are affected by the amount of time Cass holds the funds prior to payment and the dollar volume processed. Both the number of transactions processed and the dollar volume processed are therefore key metrics followed by management. Other factors will also influence revenue and profitability, such as changes in the general level of interest rates, which have a significant effect on net interest income. The funds generated by these processing activities are invested in overnight investments, investment grade securities, advances to payees, and loans generated by the Bank. The Bank earns most of its revenue from net interest income, or the difference between the interest earned on its loans and investments and the interest paid on its deposits and other borrowings. The Bank also assesses fees on other services such as cash management services.

Industry-wide factors that impact the Company include the willingness of large corporations to outsource key business functions such as freight, energy, and environmental payment and audit. The benefits that can be achieved by outsourcing transaction processing, and the management information generated by Cass' systems can be influenced by factors such as the competitive pressures within industries to improve profitability, the general level of transportation costs and deregulation of energy costs. Economic factors that impact the Company include the general level of economic activity that can affect the volume and size of invoices processed, the ability to hire and retain qualified staff, and the growth and quality of the loan portfolio. The general level of interest rates also has a significant effect on the revenue of the Company. As discussed in greater detail in Item 7A, "Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk," a decline in the general level of interest rates can have a negative impact on net interest income and conversely, a rise in the general level of interest rates can have a positive impact on net interest income. The cost of energy is another factor that has a significant impact on the transportation and facility sectors. As the price of energy goes up or down, the Company's earnings increase or decrease with the dollar amount of transportation and facility expense invoices.

The Company continues to operate profitably, posting a 1.43% return on average assets and 14.98% return on average equity. The Company's common equity Tier 1 capital ratio was 15.10% at December 31, 2025, significantly exceeding regulatory requirements. In addition, the Company has maintained exceptional credit quality with no loan charge-offs during the year ended December 31, 2025.

The Company's solid capital and liquidity positions, combined with ongoing earnings, are expected to continue to allow for investment in strategic opportunities when they become available, in addition to return of capital to shareholders. The Company delivered $16.5 million in dividend payments and $26.0 million in share repurchases during 2025. The Company continues to invest in the technology, processes, and people required to support its multi-national customer base.

Currently, management views Cass' major opportunity as the continued expansion of its payment and information processing service offerings and customer base. Management intends to accomplish this by maintaining the Company's leadership position in applied technology, which when combined with the security and processing controls of the Bank, makes Cass unique in the industry.

paragraphs: Cass Information Systems, Inc. ("Cass" or the "Company") 提供支付及資訊處理服務給美國的大型製造、流通與零售企業。本公司服務包括貨運發票評估、支付處理、審計以及會計與運輸資訊的產生。Cass 也會處理並支付與設施相關的發票，包括電力與天然氣以及廢棄物與電信費用。Cass 解決方案包括整合式支付，為需要敏捷金融科技夥伴的客戶提供 B2B 支付平台。此外，本公司提供教會管理軟體解決方案以及線上平台，用以提供信仰基於與非營利組織的慷慨服務。本公司銀行子公司 Cass Commercial Bank ("Bank") 支持本公司的支付作業。Bank 也為其目標市場提供銀行服務，包括美國聖路易斯都會區的私人持有企業與餐廳特許經營權及信仰基於事工。

於 2025 年 4 月 7 日，本公司與 Asignet USA Inc ("Asignet") 簽訂資產買賣協議，將其電信費用管理與受管理移動解決方案業務單位 ("TEM Business Unit") 售出，買價為 18.0 百萬美元。交易於 2025 年 6 月 30 日完成。本公司也與 Asignet 簽訂過渡服務協議，提供資訊科技、資料吸入及支付處理服務，期限不超過交易完成後 18 個月。
Cass 是一家資訊服務公司，主要專注於為美國的大型企業處理應付款及相關交易。Cass 擁有四項核心專長，涵蓋其大部分的處理服務。

資料取得 – 這指的是從多樣化、異質來源收集資料元素，並為客戶建立完整的資料庫。資料是資訊經濟的原始材料。Cass 從複雜且多樣的輸入文件、電子媒體、專有資料庫及資料來源取得關鍵資料，包括從供應商發票以及客戶採購與銷售系統取得的資料。透過其多種取得原始資料的方法，包括由人工智慧 ("AI") 支援的方法，Cass 能將關鍵資料組合至集中式資料管理系統與資料倉儲，從而產生一個資訊引擎，用以管理關鍵企業功能與處理系統的動力。
資料管理 – 一旦資料被組合，Cass 能利用衍生資訊的動力為客戶產生顯著的節省與效益。此資訊被整合至客戶獨特的財務與會計系統，消除內部會計處理的需要，並為這些關鍵系統提供內部與外部支援。資訊也用來產生管理與例外報告，用以進行作業控制、反饋、規劃協助與績效衡量。
商業智慧 – 在正確的時間、正確的地點以及正確的格式接收資訊對企業生存至關重要。Cass 的資訊交付解決方案提供報告、數位影像、資料檔與檢索功能，透過網路或直接輸入客戶內部系統。Cass 的專有網路管理交付系統是驅動這些關鍵功能的基礎。交易、作業、控制、狀態與處理例外資訊皆透過此係統交付，為 Cass 客戶創造一個高效、可存取且高度可靠的資產。
財務交換 – 因為 Cass 在競爭對手中獨特之處在於擁有商業銀行，因此也能管理客戶資金至其供應商的流動。這是區別特徵，顯然需要銀行機構的處理能力、作業系統與財務完整性。Cass 提供立即、準確、受控且受保護的資金管理與資金轉移系統能力給所有客戶。舊有的昂貴支票處理與交付機制被更高效的電子現金管理與資金轉移系統取代。
Cass 的核心專長使其能以整合、高效且系統化的方式處理最高交易量。不僅如此，Cass 能處理交易，也能收集定義交易的資料，並執行規範其條款的財務支付。
這些核心競爭優勢，透過共享的商業流程加以強化，驅動 Cass 的戰略業務單位。基於這些基礎，Cass 繼續探尋能運用這些競爭優勢與流程的新業務機會。

本公司透過其運輸資訊服務業務單位，是美國運輸發票處理與付款產業中，根據總付款金額與處理項目數量而言規模最大的公司之一。競爭對手包括少數主要競爭者與散佈於美國各地的許多小型運輸發票審計公司。雖然這些審計公司提供運輸付款服務，但少數公司並未在全國範圍內競爭。這些競爭者主要以價格、功能與服務水準進行競爭。本公司透過其設施費用管理業務單位，也與位於美國各地、支付公用事業費用並提供管理報告的其他公司競爭。可取得的資料顯示，本公司是提供公用事業資訊處理與付款服務的最主要供應商之一。Cass 在這些競爭者中獨特之處在於，並未獨佔任何一家能源服務供應商（"ESP"）的關係。多個 ESP 廣告本公司服務，並以其獨特的審計、諮詢與科技能力增加價值。許多 Cass 的服務是根據 ESP 定製，提供完整的解決方案，而無需 ESP 進行任何開發成本。本公司 TouchPoint 部門提供教會管理軟體解決方案與線上平台，用以為基於信仰的組織與非營利機構提供慷慨服務，這是一項與銀行基於信仰的客戶相關的補充服務。此外，本公司透過其 CassPay 操作，與企業付款解決方案供應商競爭。

銀行設立為密蘇裏州的信託公司，擁有銀行業務權限，並於 1906 年成立。本公司最初因其擁有 federally-insured 商業銀行而被歸類為銀行控股公司，並於 1982 年在密蘇裏州法律下成立為 Cass Commercial Corporation。於 1983 年 2 月獲得聯邦儲備委員會（"FRB"）批准。本公司於 2001 年 1 月將名稱改為 Cass Information Systems, Inc.。於 2011 年 12 月，聖路易斯聯邦儲備銀行（"FRB"）批准 Cass Information Systems, Inc. 選舉成為金融控股公司。作為金融控股公司，Cass 可從事屬於金融性質或與金融活動相關的業務。銀行面臨來自聖路易斯、密蘇裏州都會區及其他競爭地區的許多銀行與金融機構的競爭。然而，銀行的主要競爭對手為能透過廣泛分行網路提供廣泛銀行與相關服務的大型銀行控股公司。銀行針對位於聖路易斯、密蘇裏州及其他選定美國城市的私人企業、餐廳連鎖店與基於信仰的機構提供服務。

本公司持有若干專利，用以提供付款與評價服務。這些包括：FreightPay®、Transdata®、Ratemaker®、Best Rate®、Rate Exchange®、CassPort®、Cass Freight Index®、Cass Truckload Linehaul Index®、Cass Intermodal Price Index®、Expense$mart®、ExpenseSmart®、TouchPoint®、Gyve®、Generosity Made Simple®、WasteVision™、AcuAudit™ 和 Direct2Carrier Payments™。本公司也持有專利，用以管理員工負擔費用、通訊費用管理資訊、電子審計以及電子產生與分析運輸參數的方法與系統。本公司也持有用於電子審計的電腦可讀取媒體專利。
本公司及其子公司擁有多樣化的客戶羣，並未依賴任何單一客戶或客戶羣組，以對其業務產生重大影響。
本公司及其子公司截至 2026 年 2 月 27 日，擁有 860 名全職與 156 名兼職員工，不計已終止的業務。這些員工中，銀行擁有 68 名全職與 0 名兼職員工。

paragraphs: 針對每個客戶所提供的特定付款及資訊處理服務，皆為個別開發以符合各客戶的需求，而這些需求可能差異極大。此外，客戶及產業間在自動化程度如電子資料交換、影像處理、作業流程及基於網路的解決方案方面，亦有極大的差異。這些因素結合後，使得客戶之間的定價差異極大。然而，總體而言，Cass 透過服務費用、交易層級付款服務及付款過程產生的帳戶餘額投資，來獲取其處理服務的報酬。服務費用的金額、類型及計算方式因服務內容而異，但通常會依照處理的交易量來計算。交易層級付款服務及付款處理週期中產生的餘額所產生的利息收入，會受到 Cass 在付款前持有資金時間長短及處理的金額所影響。因此，處理的交易數量及處理的金額，為管理層所關注的關鍵指標。其他因素也會影響收入及獲利能力，例如總體經濟中利率的一般水平，對淨利息收入有顯著影響。這些處理活動所產生的資金，會投資於隔夜投資、投資等級證券、支付給收款人的貸款，以及銀行所產生的貸款。銀行大部分的收入來自於淨利息收入，即其貸款及投資所賺取的利息與其存款及其他借款所支付的利息之間的差額。銀行也會對其他服務如現金管理服務收取費用。

影響本公司的產業因素包括大型企業願意委外關鍵業務功能如運輸、能源及環境付款與稽核的意願。委外處理交易的效益，以及 Cass 系統所產生的管理資訊，會受到產業內競爭壓力以提高獲利能力、運輸成本的一般水平及能源成本的放鬆管制等因素的影響。影響本公司的經濟因素包括經濟活動的一般水平，這可能影響處理的發票數量及規模、聘僱及留住合格員工的能力，以及貸款組合的成長與品質。總體經濟中利率的一般水平也會對本公司的收入產生顯著影響。如 Item 7A 所討論的更詳細內容，「市場風險的量化與質化揭露」，總體經濟中利率水平的下降可能對淨利息收入產生負面影響，反之，總體經濟中利率水平的上升則可能對淨利息收入產生正面影響。能源成本是另一個對運輸及設施產業產生顯著影響的因素。當能源價格上漲或下跌時，本公司的獲利也會隨運輸及設施費用發票的美元金額而增加或減少。
本公司持續營運獲利，達成 1.43% 的平均資產回報率及 14.98% 的平均權益回報率。本公司普通股一級資本比率在 2025 年 12 月 31 日為 15.10%，遠高於監管要求。此外，本公司在 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年內維持了優異的信用品質，且無貸款核銷。
本公司的強固資本與流動性地位，加上持續的獲利，預期將持續允許在有機會時進行戰略投資，並回饋資本給股東。本公司在 2025 年提供了 16.5 百萬美元的股息支付及 26.0 百萬美元的股票回購。本公司持續投資於支援其多國客戶基礎所需的科技、流程及人力。
目前，管理層認為 Cass 的主要機會是持續擴大其付款及資訊處理服務內容與客戶基礎。管理層有意透過維持本公司在應用科技方面的領導地位，來達成此目標，而此領導地位結合銀行的安全與處理控制，使 Cass 在業界獨樹一格。

headings: 金融市場與總體經濟及政治狀況的波動可能影響本公司

本公司的信用減損撥備（"ACL"）會持續評估，可能不足。
利率波動可能影響 Cass 的淨利息收入與資產負債表。
在某些情況下，Cass 會在收到客戶資金前支付發票。因此，若客戶未支付資金，Cass 可能會蒙受損失。
Cass 會將 AI 用於其業務及運作，這使其面臨內在風險，這些風險可能導致本公司遭受重大損失。
本公司面臨與處理客戶資金相關的風險。
本公司可能因原油及總體能源價格變動而受到負面影響。
本公司可能因運輸費用率變動而受到負面影響。
本公司網路科技及基礎建設若發生中斷或效能問題，可能對其業務及營運成果造成負面影響。
營運困難或網路安全問題可能損害 Cass 的聲譽及業務。
Cass 必須回應快速的科技變革，而這些變革可能比預期更困難或成本更高。
降低風險敞口的方法可能無法達到預期效果。
客戶借款、償還、投資、存款及應付款項處理作法可能與預期不同。
Cass 所在市場的競爭產品與價格壓力可能產生變化。
管理階層維持並擴展客戶關係的能力可能與預期不同。
本公司面臨流動性風險。
管理階層保留關鍵高階主管及員工的能力可能產生變化。
Cass 的股票價格可能波動且大幅變動，反應多種因素。
本公司受政府嚴格監管及監督，並可能面臨執行或其它法律行動，可能對 Cass 的業務產生不利影響。
Cass 可能會受到稅務機關的審查與挑戰，若無法有利於本公司，可能會對本公司的財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
本公司之商譽及其他無形資產之價值，未來可能下降。

paragraphs: 本節說明特定風險，這些風險可能影響本公司的業務。雖然本節試圖強調關鍵因素，請注意未來可能有其他風險變得重要。新風險可能隨時出現，而 Cass 無法預測這些風險或估計它們可能對本公司財務表現的影響程度。本節說明本公司對可能對本公司及其業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生重大且不利影響的因素的觀點。所有提及過去事件的參考，僅為範例，而非完整清單或表示這些事件是否曾發生過或是否可能未來發生。
除本報告其他部分討論或引用的因數外，可能導致實際結果與預期有重大差異的已識別風險包括以下內容：

本公司的成功在一定程度上取決於當地、國家及全球的經濟與政治條件，以及政府的貨幣政策。有利的商業環境通常特徵為經濟成長、有效率的資本市場、低通貨膨脹、低失業率、高企業與投資者信心，以及強勁的企業獲利。不利或不確定的經濟與市場條件可能由美國與國際經濟成長下降；企業活動或投資者與企業信心下降；信貸與資本可得性受限或成本增加；通貨膨脹或利率上升；高失業率；石油價格波動；天然災害；貿易政策與關稅；或這些因素的組合或其他因素所造成。此外，當前或預期的全球戰爭/軍事衝突、恐怖主義或其他地緣政治事件的影響，可能對金融市場與全球供應鏈產生不利影響。當前經濟條件受到近期通貨膨脹與較高利率的嚴重影響，這些影響可能透過負面影響本公司的固定成本與費用，進而影響本公司的獲利。對消費者與企業的經濟與通貨膨脹壓力，以及對經濟改善的不確定性，可能會導致消費者與企業的支出、貸款與儲蓄習慣產生變化。這些情況可能對本公司的貸款信用品質及其業務、財務狀況與營運成果產生重大不利影響。

聯邦預算赤字的擔憂，以及有關立法以支應美國政府運作及提高美國政府債務上限的政治衝突潛在可能，可能會增加美國政府違約其債務義務的機率，相關信用評級降級，或美國經濟衰退的風險。許多本公司投資的證券是由美國政府及政府機構與資助機構發行。由於不確定的國內政治環境，包括未來可能的聯邦政府停擺，聯邦政府因債務上限限制或其他未解決的政治問題而短時間內違約履行義務的可能性，投資於由聯邦政府發行或擔保的金融工具，會面臨流動性風險。最近，由於美國政府連續未能扭轉年度財政赤字擴大及利息支出成長的趨勢，穆迪將其對美國的長期發債人信用評級從 Aaa 降為 Aa1。進一步降級，或其它信用評級機構的降級，以及各國政府面臨的主權債務問題，
其他國家的情況，可能對美國及全球的財務市場與經濟狀況產生重大不利影響。
某些超出本公司控制範圍的事件，例如嚴峻天氣、自然災害、恐怖攻擊或其他敵對行動，可能對總體經濟、財務與資本市場、特定產業以及本公司產生不利影響。
